title: Fewest Rewrites to Match Letters
statement:
You get two strings s and t of the same length. In one step you may pick any position of t and overwrite its character with any other lowercase letter.

Return the fewest steps needed to make t an anagram of s, meaning the two strings use exactly the same letters the same number of times, in any order. s is never changed.

examples.why: t already has one a and one b that can stay. Rewrite c and d into the missing a and b. Comparing position by position would count 3 differences, but order does not matter.
Same letters in a different order: already an anagram.
No letter of t is useful, so every one must change.

constraints: s and t contain only lowercase English letters
hints: Order does not matter for anagrams, so only letter counts matter. Which letters of t can stay as they are?
For each letter, t can keep at most as many copies as s has. The rest of its copies must be rewritten.
Count letters in s, then walk t and use up counts. Every letter of t that finds no remaining count costs one step.

explain.intuition:
Think of s as a shopping list of letters and t as what is already in your basket. Any letter in the basket that is still on the list can stay. Everything else is surplus and has to be swapped for something missing.

Because both strings have the same length, the number of surplus letters in t equals the number of missing letters, and each step turns one surplus letter into one missing letter. So the answer is just the surplus count: for each letter, max(0, count in t − count in s), summed.
steps: Count each letter of s in an array of 26.
Walk t. If the count for its letter is positive, decrement it: that letter can stay.
Otherwise this letter is surplus; add 1 to the answer.
pitfalls: Counting positions where s[i] ≠ t[i]. Anagrams ignore order, so the first example would wrongly give 3.
Adding surplus and missing letters together, which counts every rewrite twice.

solutions.title: Sort both and match
solutions.idea: Sort both strings and walk them with two pointers, counting letters they share. Everything in t that was not matched must be rewritten.

solutions.title: Letter counts
solutions.idea: Count letters of s, then spend those counts while reading t. Letters of t with nothing left to spend are surplus.

followups: The strings may have different lengths, and you may also change s. What is the fewest total rewrites to make them anagrams?
The alphabet is all of Unicode. What do you use instead of an array of 26?
lcTitle: Minimum Number of Steps to Make Two Strings Anagram
